ground_truth.location: Table 5, Panel A (Number of Cosponsors), row All, column 1 (OLS - full sample)
ground_truth.context: Table 5 ("RD and PS Matching Estimates"), Panel A, all sponsors, column 1.  Bill-level OLS regression, U.S. House public bills of the 101st-111th Congresses; dependent variable: the number of cosponsors on the bill; regressor of interest: a dummy for a female sponsor (the table entry is its coefficient).  Controls: Congress fixed effects; bill characteristics (dummies for the committee of referral and for the minor topic); sponsor characteristics (age, tenure in Congress, rookie, committee leader — chair or ranking member — black, party dummy, occupational dummies, Ivy League degree, born in the state of election, total number of bills sponsored in the Congress); district characteristics (macro-area dummies, percent black, over-65, foreign-born and urban residents, log median income, log population density).  Robust standard errors clustered at the individual-Congress (sponsor-term) level.

i4r.notes: Meta-database row 1391 (Change inference; DP75 Table 3): 1.395, SE 1.025 clustered by member (p = 0.174; loses significance). Amended controls (row 1415, DP75 Table 2): 1.370 (0.638).  Adding Congresses 112-116 (row 1435): 2.509 (0.675).

cell.label: claude-code
deviations_manifest: Percent of opposite-party cosponsors: used the dataset's pct_cosponsors_opposite, which equals opposite-party cosponsors / cosponsors (sponsor not in the denominator, missing for bills with zero cosponsors), multiplied by 100. The paper's text describes the denominator as cosponsors plus sponsor; the shipped variable was used as the authors' constructed outcome.

Propensity scores estimated by probit at the bill level (the paper's text does not say probit vs logit); ATE inverse-probability weights (1/p for women, 1/(1-p) for men). PS estimated separately within each party sample.

RD columns use the bandwidths stated in the task for these rows (13 for Republicans Panel A col 3; 24 for Democrats Panel B col 2), uniform kernel, linear in the margin with slope differing at the threshold. CCT mserd bandwidths recomputed on bills (17.79 and 16.45) are printed as diagnostics only.

Column 3 PS: district characteristics only (3 region dummies, % black, % over 65, % foreign born, % urban, log median income, log population density), estimated within the bandwidth; outcome regression adds Congress FE and bill characteristics.
Columns 4/5 PS: district characteristics + margin of victory of the elected candidate (|MV1_democrat|) (+ sponsor characteristics in col 5); bills with missing MV1_democrat dropped.

Macro regions built from ICPSR state codes (Northeast <20, Midwest 20-39, South 40-59, West 60+). Log population density = lnpop - ln(area in sq. miles); lnarea is stored in square meters for Congresses 108-111 (and a few earlier districts) and was converted to square miles.

Occupational dummies: occ1-occ5 (education, lawyer, professional, business, agriculture), with unknown and miscellaneous as base. Party dummy entered as factor of sponsor_party (Dem/Rep/independent) in the pooled sample. Total bills sponsored = count of bills per sponsor-Congress in the sample with a matched sponsor.

Minor topic and Congress absorbed as fixed effects (fixest); fixest drops fixed-effect singletons (1 bill in the all-sponsor OLS), as reghdfe would. Clusters: sponsor-Congress (Congress x state x district x seat order).
deviations_stdout: percent of opposite-party cosponsors uses the dataset's pct_cosponsors_opposite (opposite/cosponsors, sponsor not in denominator) x100; propensity scores are probit at bill level with ATE inverse-probability weights; RD bandwidths are the ones stated for these rows (13, 24) with a uniform kernel.
cell.notes: Data: AnalysisData/bills_analysis_101-111_replication.dta, restricted to bills with a matched sponsor (61,334). Two exploratory runs (variable listing; checks of the pct variable, region codes, lnarea units). One estimation run, which is final. Column 1 OLS: outcome on female dummy + Congress FE + 226 minor topic FE + 33 committee-of-referral dummies + sponsor characteristics (age, tenure, rookie, committee chair/ranking member, black, party, 5 occupation dummies, Ivy League, born in state, bills sponsored in Congress) + district characteristics; SE clustered by sponsor-Congress. While reading the paper's method sections I incidentally saw some Table 3 and Table 4 numbers in the garbled text (Table 3 columns 1-4, including n. bills 61,334 for those columns; Table 5's numbers were not viewed); no specification choice was tuned toward them. No author scripts or output files in the dataset were opened.
